comparison: Both evaluate reentrant behavior for Caprin1 vs monotonic behavior for pY-Caprin1 (C2, C3, C30, C31, C79, C80). Both find SUPPORTED with convergent evidence across multiple methods. OpenEval emphasizes consistency across experimental and three computational approaches; peer reviewers explicitly affirm the models 'provide convincing evidence' and 'reproduce two observed trends.'

Both evaluate Na+ depletion in Caprin1 condensates (C32, C33, C34, C52, C54). Both find SUPPORTED with agreement across rG-RPA, experiments, and MD simulations. OpenEval notes experimental depletion exceeds predictions; peer reviewers accept 'predicted trends generally in line with measurement' without challenging the discrepancy.

Both evaluate pY-Caprin1's distinct ion partitioning behavior (C35, C36, C53, C55). Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes Na+ enhancement and fundamental differences from Caprin1; peer reviewers accept these as part of comprehensive charge-dependent characterization, noting distinction is 'captured by a two component model and also when salt ions are explicitly modeled.'

Both evaluate Cl⁻-mediated bridging mechanism (C4, C56-C61). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with quantitative MD analysis showing 98.5% Cl⁻ near Arg+ and ~80% true bridging. Peer reviewers find UNCERTAIN - Reviewer 2 challenges interpretation, requesting analysis to 'distinguish net charge neutralization and interchain bridging,' suggesting alternative explanation of simple charge neutralization.

Both evaluate ATP-Mg colocalization (C5, C45, C46, C48, C67, C72, C73, C77, C78). Both find SUPPORTED with convergence of experimental measurements (5-60 fold enhancement) and theoretical predictions. Peer reviewers note 'FTS provides insights into the co-localization of ions and proteins that is consistent with NMR' and experimental validation in Table 2 is not challenged.

Both evaluate MD predictions for RtoK mutants (C62, C63, C65). Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes MD correctly predicts experimental rank order and acknowledges discrepancy for reentrant dissolution. Peer reviewers accept predictions as 'consistent with the measurement' and treat explanation for high-salt discrepancy as reasonable.

Both evaluate rG-RPA predictions about counterion valency effects (C38-C42, C44). Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes internal consistency with polymer physics principles; peer reviewers praise comprehensive theoretical framework, stating models 'provide convincing evidence' and 'application of this theory to multivalent ions reveals many interesting features.' Counterintuitive Na+ attraction prediction not challenged.

Both evaluate sequence characterization data (C16-C21). Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes support from direct sequence analysis, mass spectrometry, and straightforward calculations. Peer reviewers accept these as factual characterizations forming basis for understanding charge-dependent behaviors; no reviewer questions the analysis.

Both evaluate rG-RPA+FH predictions vs experimental observations (C23-C26). Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes good agreement between theoretical predictions and cited experimental work. Peer reviewers accept predictions as consistent with experimental data, noting theory 'reproduce two observed trends' and 'predicted trends are generally in line with the measurement.'

Both evaluate mechanistic interpretation distinguishing Caprin1 vs pY-Caprin1 behavior (C82). Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes interpretation well-supported by charge properties and consistent phase behavior differences. Peer Reviewer 2 explicitly supports classification into 'high net charge' vs 'screening' classes as explaining observed behaviors.

Both address MD simulation results (C49 in peer review overlaps with C2, C3, C30, C31, C47, C49, C66, C79 in OpenEval). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED emphasizing convergent evidence. Peer reviewers find UNCERTAIN - Reviewer 1 notes 'modeling at the coarse-grained level misses key effects' including salt-backbone coordination and pi-interactions, suggesting CG approach may miss important mechanisms despite general consistency.

Partial overlap on FTS results (C66, C72, C73). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as part of ATP-Mg colocalization evidence. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, noting 'FTS is well suited to handle this complexity' and robustness across FTS model variations is not challenged.
